Throughout the United States, foul weather such as hurricanes, tornadoes, and ice storms harm the electric grid today. If parts of the grid go out of service, the rail network will not be able to operate. Also, the foul weather can harm the catenary infrastructure, which will also stop the movement of goods and people until repaired. Climate change may exacerbate the impacts of these weather risks on catenary systems in certain locations. Resilient infrastructure should be built with this in mind.
